results.title: Domaine Rebourgeon-Mure | Cru Wines, LLC
results.rawContent:
From their domaine in Pommard, the Rebourgeons tend 18 acres, divided between many well regarded holdings in the appellations of Beaune, Volnay and Pommard, planted entirely in Pinot Noir and averaging more than 40 years with the oldest parcels of Pommard planted in 1902. The viticultural and winemaking methods have not changed much in the last five centuries: Responsible farming, manual harvest, and an aim to make elegant wines with ability to age.
Daniel Rebourgeon and his son David own and operate one of the oldest estates in Pommard, started by their ancestor Jean Bourgogne in 1552 who had taken a 99 year lease to raise vines at the holy abbey, Marguerite of Bouillard.

There are many Premier Crus in Burgundy, but nowhere more so than in Pommard, where there are 125 hectares of Premier Cru vineyards, spread across 28 different climats.
Les Arvelets covers 8.45 hectares, but our plot is located within the Clos des Arvelets, of which our family owned the entirety — 3.30 hectares.
Until 1763, it belonged to Mr. Micault d’Harvelay (who took his name from the Clos des Arvelets), Lord of Pommard, Squire, Secretary to the King, Fermier Général, and Director of Powder and Saltpeter for the Kingdom. After that, it became the property of the Marey-Monge family, who held it until 1926, when this plot was acquired.
Subsequently divided through family inheritances, this clos — enclosed by walls (up to 4 meters high!) — is situated on terraced land with full southern exposure.
Very steep, with a 20% incline and occasional cross slopes, this vineyard is cultivated by hand and produces a wine with a ruby color, a concentrated and pleasant nose, and soft, well-integrated tannins.
The viticultural and winemaking methods have not changed much in the last five centuries: Responsible farming, manual harvest, and the aim is to make elegant wines with the ability to age. The yield is controlled, and the focus is on the maturation of the grape. All of the grapes are 100% de-stemmed and inspected in the cellar before going into temperature controlled cement tanks for a 5 day cold pre fermentation.The aging is carried out in a cellar underneath the winery in oak barrels, no more than 1/3 new oak for 14 to 18 months, before they are estate bottled.

Planting Years: 1901, 1925

Altitude: 245 meters

Les Charmots is located on a hillside with particularly good South to South-East exposure.
In terms of both reputation and size (9 hectares, 64 ares), it ranks third among the Premier Cru vineyards of Pommard. Enclosed by a stone wall, Clos Des Charmots is an old vineyard of fine Pinot Noir vines, planted in 1901 and 1925. Its wine is born from soil that stands out through very subtle nuances—light, red, and stony.
A rich and silky wine, aromatic and complex. It is of great finesse, both in its fruity aromas and its flavors. On the palate, it is round and deep.
The viticultural and winemaking methods have not changed much in the last five centuries: Responsible farming, manual harvest, and the aim is to make elegant wines with the ability to age. The yield is controlled, and the focus is on the maturation of the grape. South-South East exposure, All of the grapes are 100% destemmed and inspected in the cellar before going into temperature controlled cement tanks for a 5 day cold pre fermentation. The aging is carried out in a cellar underneath the winery in oak barrels, no more than 1/3 new oak for 14 to 18 months, before they are estate bottled.
"Beautiful light red robe and a nose offering a fine blend of red fruit aromas with hints of oak. On the palate, the wine is described as young, dense, tannic, and still tightly wound, indicating a high-level structure built for aging. Patience is recommended. 93/100 Gilbert & Gaillard.

Volnay, perched on the hill of Chaignot high up in the Côte de Beaune, occupies a narrow and steeply sloping site as if to allow more space to the vines. The hill itself is oriented slightly differently from the general run of the country so that the vines face South-East rather than East. These vineyards have been valued and exploited for centuries. Long before the Revolution the harvests of Volnay went to the Knights of Malta, the Abbeys of Saint-Andoche d’Autun and Maizières, or to the Dukes of Bourgogne and their successors, the Kings of France.
The oolitic limestone has a superficial similarity to the reddish igneous rock (porphyry) found in the Morvan district. It is pink in color with pale green inclusions and overlain by banks of schist. At the top of the slope, this limestone predominates. Lower down we find white, chalky-textured argovien limestone. Lower still are reddish Bathonien limestone, pebbly and ferruginous. The soils at the foot of the slope are deeper and more gravelly. Altitudes: 230-280 meters.
"A bright fresh purple. Again the bouquet is slightly reticent but there is a fine concentration of brisk red berry fruit on the palate, good acidity, and currently a firmer finish. No worries about the potential but needs time. Drink from 2028-2033." Tasted October 2023. - Jasper Morris
92/100 Gilbert & Gaillard

Medium to full-bodied, pure and mineral, with lively acids and delicately chalky tannins, it's a blend of very old vines in Pluchots with Lurets, including some premier cru fruit." - Wine Advocate, Robert Parker, January 18, 2024

results.title: Domaine de la Ferme Saint-Martin | Cru Wines, LLC
results.rawContent:
The Ferme Saint Martin vineyard is located in the small village of Suzette right at the top of the Beaume de Venise Appellation Controlee. The domaine covers 89 acres of land, 56 of which are planted with Grenache, Cinsault and Syrah for the reds and Roussane and Clairette for the whites. The vines face south on a very dry and rocky terroir built in terraces between altitudes of 800 and 1600 feet. The wines are certified organic and follow very natural and strict methods of grape growing and winemaking. The most important is the natural treatment of the soil and the vine, with no chemical spraying and manual harvesting, all wines are unfiltered.
Guy Julien at La Ferme Saint-Martin has gradually turned over the reins to his son Thomas. They are crafting some of the most aromatic wines.
Certified Organic  
50% of the vineyard in biodynamic conversion
2020 Beaumes de Venise Costancia Ferme Saint Martin
DOMAINE DE LA FERME SAINT MARTIN  
2020 Beaumes de Venise Costancia
Certified Organic & Vegan
Certified organic wine, no pesticides or herbicides.Mechanically worked soils between the vines, maintenance of a plant carpet between the rows. Yield: 30 to 32hl/h.
The first selection takes place during the initial grape picking. A second selection of the grapes is made before they are crushed. The quality of the wine is determined by this selection. A very small quantity of sulfates is added to the grapes in order to facilitate the bottling, transportation and preservation of the wine. The maceration lasts 21 to 28 days, the aging 18 months in half neutral oak barrels 2 to 10 years old. Bottled without fining, filtration and no added sulfites.

results.title: Domaine de Monteils | Cru Wines, LLC
results.rawContent:
The small Sauternes region is located on the left bank of the Garonne River, about 25 miles south of Bordeaux. The soil is representative of the Garonne bed’s geological evolution, which has carried the alluvia throughout the gravel terraces. Domaine de Monteils stands at the gateway to the Sauternes region, in the parish of Preignac, one of the 5 villages (Sauternes, Bommes, Fargues, Preignac and Barsac) that have the privilege to claim the AOC Sauternes. The domaine was established in the village of Preignac in 1861 by Daniel Fiton. During the 1960s, Jean-Claude Cousin followed after his grand parents' footsteps and developed the domaine. Today, Jean-Claude’s daughter Marie-Christine Cousin and her husband Jean-Paul Fourcaud manage the domaine.

results.rawContent:
Cellar at Chateau Haut Vignoble
Cellar at Chateau Haut Vignoble
The vineyards of Château Tour Haut Vignoble lie near the Atlantic Ocean and along the Gironde estuary, benefiting from the gentle, tempering influence of the river. Situated in the northern part of Saint-Estèphe, the estate is planted on slopes composed of deep gravel and clay-limestone soils—an ideal combination that provides excellent natural drainage and steady, moderated temperatures. Though the property has been cultivated for nearly 190 years, the current vines average 36 years of age, offering both maturity and vitality.
Each grape variety is vinified and aged separately, plot by plot, to preserve the unique character of each parcel. Traditional cold pre-fermentation maceration and frequent pump-overs help extract deep color and support a clean, controlled fermentation. The estate also employs physical tangential filtration to ensure purity and finesse in the final wine.
Owned by the Braquessac family since 1860, the château continues to be managed with great respect for its land, intervening as little as possible in the vineyard. Today, the collaboration between father, an agricultural engineer, and son, an oenologist, drives a constant pursuit of quality.

results.title: Chateau Flotis | Cru Wines, LLC
results.rawContent:
Located in Castelnau d’Estretefonds, in the heart of the Fronton appellation, the domaine has been owned and operated by Cathy Ribes since 2004 (who also owns Domaine du Roc). She is constantly replacing and working the vines of varietals native to this area such as Negrette, the most noble of that region. Cathy is also working on a new cellar half of which is underground, like a cave under a cliff where they store the harvest in tanks directly by gravity.
In 2009, Cathy Ribes decided to start the organic conversion of the entire domaine which was certified in 2012. With this in mind, her wines do not see any added yeast, filtration, collage, and minimum amounts of oak aging for some cuvees. Si Noire is the flagship of the property and the result of 37 year-old vines growing on 5 acres at the highest elevation of the vineyards, adjacent to an oak forest on stony soil.
Anne is the oldest child of Frédéric and Cathy. She studied viticulture and oenology in Montpellier and is the winemaker of the estate.

results.title: Chateau des Graviers | Cru Wines, LLC
results.rawContent:
The 17 acre Bordeaux vineyard of Chateau des Graviers is located in the Arsac region of Margaux and has been in the Dufourg-Landry family for generations. Christophe Landry is the fifth generation winemaker and has been making wines since the mid-nineties.
Some of the adjacent parcels are Grands Crus Classes such as Chateau Issan, Rauzan-Ségla, Prieuré-Lichine and Marojallia. The soil dates back to the Quaternary and is made of gravel from the Pyrennees and of clay from the Garonne river bed.
Christophe purchased new plots to create Clos Dufourg, a small cru of 11 acres from several types of terroir planted with the five Bordeaux red grape varieties - Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Petit Verdot, Malbec and Carmenère . 2019 is the first vintage produced.  The subsequent construction of a new cellar made of stacked straw allows him to fully experiment with various winemaking and aging methods.
"We would like that you can feel in our bottle the purity and delicacy offered by our soil. For that we use only what nature offers us around our vineyard." - Christophe Landry

results.title: Chateau des Capucins | Cru Wines, LLC
results.rawContent:
The Chateau des Capucins (from Chateau des Arnauds)  is an old family property passed on from father to son for more than four generations. As early as 1914, Jacques Arnauds started to purchase a few parcels in the Lalande de Pomerol AOP.  He quickly realized how much potential was in that name.  Thanks to his knowledge of the terroir, all through the years, he bought the parcels that now make up the property.
Pierre Godineau, Miss Andrée Arnauds’ husband, took over the family property in 1958.  After 18 years of management, he then passed the torch to his son Sébastien who now manages the estate with his uncle Bernard.  They are dedicated to keeping up high standards and making sure that the property lives up to one’s expectations.
2020 Lalande de Pomerol Chateau des Capucins

results.title: Domaine Boissonnet | Cru Wines, LLC
results.rawContent:
The Boissonnet family has been in the town of Serrieres in the district of Ardeche since the 17th century. The family house and the underground cellars date back to 1600. The first cellar was restored by André Boissonnet, and the second cellar was found by accident in the 1990's by his son Frédéric who is the current winemaker.
Frédéric uses both cellars as the perfect place for aging their production of Saint Joseph and Condrieu. 1990 was an outstanding vintage as well as a turning point in the life of the domaine, which at the time was only comprised of five acres of red Saint Joseph: Frédéric vinified his first cuvees as he took over the domaine that year. In 1994, the domaine grew with Saint Joseph white and Condrieu followed in 1995.

results.title: Domaine de la Madone | Cru Wines, LLC
results.rawContent:
Domaine de La Madone Vineyard
Domaine de La Madone Vineyard
Domaine de la Madone is situated along the hillside of La Madone in the Beaujolais cru village of Fleurie.  Domaine de la Madone is owned and run by Arnaud Després who is the 6th generation of his family to tend to these famous hillside vineyards, taking their name from the Chapel of La Madone which was built in 1866 and is high atop the hill above the village of Fleurie.
The estate’s 42 acres sit on pink granite and enjoy ideal growing conditions for the Gamay grape due to the exceptional amounts of sunlight it receives. Jean-Marc and Arnaud are very focused on nature and the biodiversity is plentiful with bees, crickets and butterflies amongst the vines.
The winery is built into the hillside and therefore, after manual harvesting, the grapes can be moved from picking baskets to tanks and then to barrels via gravity. The top cuvees are aged in oak barrels as well as some experimentation with concrete eggs.
2023 Fleurie, cuvee Madone, Domaine de la Madone
DOMAINE DE LA MADONE  
2024 Fleurie Cuvee Madone
100% Gamay
AOP Fleurie 
The Madone cuvée represents the largest volume of the domaine's production. Vinified as a whole harvest with a fermentation of 7 to 8 days.
Harvesting is done by hand, and the wines are fermented as whole bunches in concrete tanks to preserve the freshness and unique character of each plot. The winery is integrated into the hillside, allowing gravity to gently move the wine from picking baskets to tanks and then into barrels. Some of the top cuvées are aged in oak barrels, and there's ongoing experimentation with concrete eggs. Filtration is kept to a minimum, and only a small amount of sulphur is used.
Cuvée Madone is a beautifully expressive Beaujolais made from 60 year-old Gamay vines. Bright ruby hue and an expressive, lifted nose of fresh red berries (strawberry, raspberry, cherry) layered with classic Fleurie florals like violet and subtle granite-driven minerality. The palate is supple and medium-bodied, with juicy fruit, vibrant acidity, and fine but present tannins, giving both immediate charm and gentle structure. The finish is clean, lightly spiced, and perfumed, reflecting a balanced, fruit-forward yet elegant style typical of wines from the La Madone hillside.
The 2023 Fleurie, a floral and fruit-forward Beaujolais Cru, pairs beautifully with a wide range of dishes thanks to its light body and bright acidity. It complements poultry and lighter meats such as roasted chicken, grilled pork, duck confit, veal scaloppini, and even frog legs. This wine also shines alongside creamy pastas as well as quiche and Mediterranean-inspired salads. For cheese lovers, it’s a natural match with soft varieties like brie and goat cheese, or aged options like Comté and Gruyère. Fleurie also holds its own with charcuterie, pâtés, and even grilled or sauced red meats like beef, lamb, or duck, making it an impressively versatile table companion.
Aging capacity: 2 - 3 years after bottling.
2023 Fleurie, Madone Vieilles Vignes, Domaine de la Madone
DOMAINE DE LA MADONE  
2023 Fleurie Vieilles Vignes
100% Gamay
AOP Fleurie.   This old-vine cuvée is produced from Gamay vines aged between 70 and 100 years old. Excellent exposure spread across pink granite soil. 
2023 Viognier Pied de la Rune, Domaine de la Madone
DOMAINE DE LA MADONE  
2023 IGP Viognier Pied de la Rue

Aged: 5 years.  It pairs beautifully with delicate seafood like seared scallops with lemon beurre blanc and grilled langoustines.  Poultry dishes such as roast chicken with tarragon cream sauce or duck breast with apricot glaze echo its herbal and stone fruit profile. Vegetarian options like butternut squash risotto with sage or grilled zucchini with halloumi align well with the wine’s creamy texture and subtle minerality. For cheese, fresh goat cheese with herbs or semi-firm Alpine varieties like Tomme de Savoie make excellent matches.
